column1: # The 20 SNAPSHOT-DELTA documents, measured against what actually changed.
# FABLE's ruling (OPUS-REQ-FABLE-PROVENANCE-TRANSFER-144, 9bedb5e0) classed these as sitting in a
# genuine snapshot delta: each cites a function whose per-function record differs between its
# stamped generation and the certified parent. The same ruling says WHAT differs - 19 functions
# GN158->GN160, 15 GN159->GN160, PLATE COMMENT AND TAGS ONLY, embedded EXE identical. Names,
# bodies, sizes, prototypes and calling conventions are unchanged.
# So a document here is affected only if it RELIES on the two things that moved. Measured
# Tools/work/OPUS/snapshot_delta_reliance.py - renamed then): ZERO of the 20 quote a GFZ tag
# one of their own delta functions. All 20 cite by address and argue from the body.
# The converse slice was measured separately and did find work: gen_delta_staleness.py,
# published into the kit 2026-09-14 from Tools/work/OPUS/delta_staleness.py. It looked for
# pages CALLING one of these functions unclassified - a claim a new tag falsifies - found 14
# matches, and 5 were genuinely stale and are corrected (commit ac605404).
# NO STAMP IS WRITTEN ON THIS BASIS. Snapshot-identity is FABLE's basis and is adjudicated; this
# would be a SECOND and narrower one - 'the delta is annotation text this document does not use' -
# and widening my own transfer rule over documents another agent flagged is the author certifying
# his own high-blast claim. Referred back: OPUS-REQ-FABLE-DELTA-RELIANCE-BASIS.
